title: Global sensitivity analysis of Open Systems Pharmacology Suite physiologically based pharmacokinetic models

content.abstract_summary: Tutorial paper presenting a new open-source R package (with GUI) for conducting one-at-a-time (OAT) and global sensitivity analysis (GSA) of PBPK models built in the Open Systems Pharmacology (OSP) Suite. OAT methods: local sensitivity analysis (LSA) and probabilistic uncertainty analysis (UA). GSA methods: Morris screening, Sobol variance decomposition, and EFAST. All outputs formatted per WHO IPCS regulatory standards. Demonstrated on three case studies: (1) itraconazole IV in PK-Sim; (2) UV filter dermal absorption in MoBi; (3) rifampicin-midazolam DDI in PK-Sim. Edginton group, University of Waterloo + Beiersdorf AG. CPT:PSP 2024.
key_findings: Recommended workflow: Morris screening first to identify candidate influential parameters → Sobol or EFAST variance decomposition on the surviving subset; Morris is computationally efficient and appropriate for ranking; Sobol/EFAST for quantifying parameter interactions (T_i vs. S_i gap)

OAT vs. GSA discrepancy demonstrated empirically (Case Study 2, UV filters): local sensitivity analysis identified parameter β as most influential, but uncertainty analysis and all three GSA methods found β relatively unimportant — demonstrates that OAT can give misleading conclusions and GSA is necessary for regulatory submissions

Case Study 1 (itraconazole): 5 of 28 parameters most influential (lipophilicity/log P and fraction unbound/fu of parent compound dominant); CYP3A4 Michaelis constant K_m and inhibition constant K_i not influential — useful result for PBPK model calibration prioritization

Case Study 3 (rifampicin-midazolam DDI): E_max (maximal CYP3A4 induction by rifampicin) most influential for AUC and C_max DDI ratios; significant Sobol T_i vs. S_i gaps for fu, k_cat, K_m indicate important parameter interactions — cannot be detected by OAT

Regulatory compliance: outputs formatted per WHO IPCS guidance (sensitivity classification: High/Medium/Low/Negligible); DDI ratio analysis directly addresses a key FDA/EMA PBPK submission requirement
Package provides both R script and GUI interfaces; input parameter distributions supported: uniform, log-uniform, normal, log-normal; future work: correlated parameter distributions
limitations: Parameter distribution options in initial release limited to uniform, log-uniform, normal, log-normal — no correlated parameter support; future work needed
Only three case studies demonstrated; broader validation with additional PBPK models needed
Computational cost of GSA higher than OAT — acknowledged trade-off; Morris recommended as efficient screening step before Sobol

WHO IPCS guideline defines uncertainty ratio as 95th/50th percentile (always ≥1); package uses 2.5th–97.5th CI / median (can be <1); same thresholds applied regardless — minor methodological deviation from WHO standard

extracted_claims.text: Sensitivity analysis...is a requirement in PBPK reports submitted to regulatory agencies.

The illustrative examples presented here discuss the potential role of global sensitivity methods in identifying influential parameters that may not be detected through local sensitivity analyses alone.

The local sensitivity analysis suggests that the plasma AUC of both octocrylene and oxybenzone are strongly influenced by parameter [β]. However, the uncertainty analysis shows that when the influence of each parameter is examined over its entire range, parameter [β] has a relatively small influence.
The package not only ensures compliance with regulatory requirements for PBPK submissions but also enhances the depth of insights derived from sensitivity analyses.

numerical_findings.description: Number of PBPK model parameters analyzed in itraconazole case study

gaps_addressed: Fills the GSA/Sobol gap for PBPK identified in the work stream analysis: provides a practical open-source tool (R package + GUI) for conducting Morris, Sobol, and EFAST analyses on OSP Suite PBPK models — directly actionable for WG members doing PBPK work

Connects to chenel_2026 (ICH M15 PBPK regulatory requirements): Najjar provides the computational methodology for the GSA that chenel_2026 identifies as required for regulatory PBPK submissions; the two papers complement each other directly

Demonstrates OAT vs. GSA discrepancy with concrete example: provides the WG a publishable argument that global SA should replace local SA as the standard for PBPK submissions — relevant to the MCS SIG's mathematical rigor positioning

Open access. Edginton A = U Waterloo + Systems In Silico Ltd (corresponding); Najjar A + Krause S + Schepky A = Beiersdorf AG (Hamburg); Hamadeh A = U Waterloo + Systems In Silico. R package hosted on GitHub (exact name not parsed from full text). Package PKML files for all 3 case studies included. The itraconazole model (Hanke et al.) and midazolam/rifampicin models are publicly available from OSP GitHub — directly downloadable by WG members. Connect to chenel_2026 which identified GSA as necessary for ICH M15 regulatory submissions.
